summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of end-stage renal disease, polycystic kidney disease, atrial fibrillation, and chronic diastolic heart failure was admitted with fever and shaking chills following a dialysis session. She reported chronic band-like back pain and new right flank discomfort. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and elevated lactate, with blood cultures later confirming Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia. The source of infection remained unidentified despite imaging and AV fistula assessment. She was treated with intravenous cefepime, transitioned to cefazolin based on sensitivities, to be completed over two weeks post-dialysis. Her anticoagulation was adjusted due to antibiotic effects on coagulation, and she was restarted on warfarin at a reduced dose. A transthoracic echocardiogram showed new moderate aortic stenosis and worsening mitral regurgitation, but no vegetations. She improved clinically with resolution of fever and negative repeat blood cultures. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for antibiotic completion at her dialysis clinic, INR monitoring, and outpatient follow-up.
